source_facts.fact: stop() before every selector/drain loop; os.read cap131072B, actual read count/length not recorded. At most one positive stdout read per loop.
Every guard calls disk_usage, reads events.jsonl, discovers owned members, then reads /proc/<pid>/status RSS.
_all_members enumerates ALL /proc/[0-9]*/stat and reads each visible process stat per invocation; called by per-drain guard.
Consumer requires one CPU/nice19; Popen has no affinity override so parent capture/gzip and child producer share CPU2.
select(.05) is a maximum idle wait, not fixed50ms sleep. deadline-1 reserves cleanup time;499.038s is consistent with that rule.
Synchronous gzip1,mtime0,10000-record chunks:20680000 rawB normally/20680036 first. memoryview slices split boundaries; no Python per-record unpack loop or gzip flush per record.
Three raw SHA256 passes: outer digest, writer global digest, per-chunk digest. Two global digests receive identical incoming data.
Each close synchronously flushes/fsyncs chunk, re-reads compressed file for SHA, then fsyncs ledger. Final index separately fsynced; all in pump thread.
os.read allocates bytes; writer uses memoryview slices without explicit whole-payload copies. Header copy<=36B; stderr accumulation<=16384B. Compression/internal allocation cost unmeasured.
Sealed-input prehash happens before capture start. Cross-arm decompression/comparison only after all captures return; did not run before baseline timeout.
